objects.description: Represents a 1D angular measure stored internally as radians (double). Provides factory methods from radians, degrees, and E5/E6/E7 integer degree scales; arithmetic, comparisons, trig helpers, normalization to (-180, 180] degrees; conversions to E5/E6/E7 with rounding; and streaming via operator<< (declared here). Includes a nested SinCosPair POD and a nested Coder class for S2 coding. Constructible from two S2Point or two S2LatLng values as the spherical distance between them. Ownership semantics: trivially copyable/value type; no special destruction requirements.

Details of memory ownership and destruction follow normal C++ class semantics (no special destruction needed).

Represents a point on the unit sphere as latitude/longitude angles. Stores coordinates internally as an R2Point of radians. Provides constructors from angles and S2Point, normalization, encoding/decoding, conversion to S2Point, distance, arithmetic, comparisons, and hashing support. Latitude is in [-90,90] and longitude in [-180,180] when normalized. Ownership: value type; no dynamic resources. Construction: via public constructors or static From* helpers. Destruction: trivial.

A spherical cap region on the unit sphere, defined by a unit-length center S2Point and an angular radius stored as S1ChordAngle. Implements S2Region. Provides construction from point/height/area, queries (containment, intersection), expansion/union, centroid/area, encoding/decoding, and bounds over S2 cells/rects. Center is unit length; radius negative => empty; radius >= pi (length2==4) => full.

Opaque 64-bit identifier for S2 hierarchical cells on the sphere, with rich utilities for traversal, neighborhood, encoding/decoding, and geometry conversions. It is copyable and lightweight; id()==0 denotes invalid. Provides constructors from raw id, S2Point, and S2LatLng, and many helpers for hierarchy and Hilbert-curve navigation.
Legacy coder nested in S2CellId that serializes S2CellId via its token representation using s2coding::S2Coder interface.
Hash functor wrapper for S2CellId for legacy compatibility with hash containers not using absl::Hash natively.

Concrete S2Region representing a single S2 hierarchical cell on the unit sphere. Provides geometry (vertices, edges, center), subdivision into 4 children, approximate and exact areas, distance queries to points/edges/cells, and region-interface bounds/containment/intersection. Constructed from S2CellId or convenience constructors from S2Point/S2LatLng; also static factories FromFace and FromFacePosLevel. Non-POD (virtuals) but copyable by value. Ownership: holds S2CellId and its UV rectangle. Destruction is trivial; no custom destructor. Unknown details: implementations of several methods are defined elsewhere.
Enumeration of the four canonical cell boundaries/edges in UV order within a face: bottom, right, top, left. Used to index vertices/edges and derive constant U/V or I/J coordinates along an edge.

Axis-aligned, closed rectangle in 2D Euclidean space (R^2). Stores two R1Interval bounds (x and y). Provides constructors from points or intervals, emptiness/validity checks, geometric queries (containment, intersection), accessors, and expansion/union/intersection operations. Copyable by value; no special ownership semantics. Note: FromCenterSize is declared here but its definition is not present in this header. Destruction is trivial as it has only value-type members. Empty rectangles are represented by both x and y intervals being empty; validity requires both bounds to be simultaneously empty or non-empty.

Configuration container for S2Builder controlling snapping behavior, crossing handling, simplification, idempotency, intersection tolerance, and memory tracking.

Enum policy in GraphOptions controlling how reverse-edge pairs are handled for different layer semantics.

Represents a polygonal S2Region on the unit sphere, composed of zero or more non-crossing S2Loop shells/holes. Provides robust geometric operations (union, intersection, difference, XOR), snapping/simplification, distance/projection queries, containment/intersection tests with polygons, polylines, and cells, encoding/decoding, and an embedded S2Shape for indexing. Loops are stored in canonical preorder, with hierarchy and bounds cached; a MutableS2ShapeIndex backs advanced queries.
S2Shape adapter that exposes an S2Polygon to S2ShapeIndex. Edges are directed with interior on the left. Does not own the polygon; lifetime must outlive the index unless using OwningShape.

S2Shape adapter that owns the S2Polygon. Useful for indexing transient polygons; the index deletes the shape and thus the polygon when done. Supports decoding itself from a Decoder by decoding an embedded S2Polygon.

Represents a geodesic polyline on the unit sphere: an ordered sequence of vertices connected by straight S2 edges. Provides construction from points/lat-lngs, snapping/simplifying, geometric queries (length, centroid, interpolation, projection, intersection), polyline simplification, region interface, and encoding/decoding. Vertices must be unit length; adjacent vertices must not be identical or antipodal. Includes nested S2Shape wrappers for indexing with S2ShapeIndex, including an owning variant that manages the polyline lifetime.
Non-owning S2Shape adapter for S2Polyline, to insert a polyline into an S2ShapeIndex. Holds a raw pointer to an external S2Polyline; lifetime must outlive the Shape unless using OwningShape.

Owning S2Shape adapter that stores a unique_ptr to an S2Polyline and transfers its lifetime to the S2ShapeIndex. Provides Init from unique_ptr and a decoder-based constructor to build the polyline directly from serialized data.

Nested configuration type for S2RegionCoverer. Holds constraints for coverings such as maximum number of cells, min/max cell levels, and level modulation. Provides accessors/mutators and a helper to compute the effective maximum level. Construction/destruction follow normal C++ object semantics; no special ownership constraints are defined here.

Main class that computes coverings of S2Region objects using S2CellIds under configurable constraints. It is movable but not copyable. Provides methods to generate coverings, interior coverings, a faster approximate covering, flood-fill style coverings, and to validate/canonicalize coverings. Lifecycle: default construct or construct with Options; no explicit destruction requirements beyond destructor.

S2Loop is a simple spherical polygon loop (single closed chain of S2Point vertices with implicit closure). It models S2Region and provides geometry operations: containment, intersection, distance, area/centroid/curvature, encoding/decoding, and indexing via MutableS2ShapeIndex. Special one-vertex forms represent empty and full loops. Supports normalization, inversion, and constructing regular loops. It also exposes nested Shape classes for S2ShapeIndex integration. Destruction is automatic; copies are via Clone or move semantics; assignment copy is deleted.

Wrapper S2Shape for indexing an S2Loop in an S2ShapeIndex without taking ownership of the loop. Exposes the loop edges and reference point to the index API. Initialize with Init(const S2Loop*). Lifetime of the referenced S2Loop must exceed the Shape’s lifetime.

S2Shape wrapper that owns the S2Loop memory; when the shape is destroyed by S2ShapeIndex, the loop is deleted. Use when constructing a loop solely for indexing. Initialize with a unique_ptr to a const S2Loop.

Abstract base class representing polygonal geometry on the sphere as a collection of edges with optional interior. It defines nested helper structs and iterator/range types for accessing edges, chains, and vertices. Used as the common interface for points, polylines, and polygons in S2. Construction is via derived types; this header does not provide concrete constructors. Encoding is optionally supported via overriding Encode and type_tag.
Represents a directed edge between two S2Points. Degenerate edges can represent points. Provides helpers to reverse, test degeneracy, and vertex incidence; supports hashing and comparisons.
Identifies a contiguous range of edge ids forming a chain within a shape, using start and length.
Specifies the position of an edge within a chain via chain_id and offset.
Pairs a sample S2Point with a boolean indicating whether it lies inside the shape; used as a seed for containment tests.
Forward iterator over the vertices of a specific chain within an S2Shape. Holds a non-owning pointer to the shape and caches edges for efficiency.
View providing begin/end iterators over the vertices of a given chain of a shape; does not own the shape.
Forward iterator over the chains of an S2Shape. Non-owning; dereferences to a Chain descriptor.
Range facade exposing begin/end to iterate all chains of an S2Shape using ChainIterator.

functions.name: s2textformat::ParsePoints

requirements: vertices must be non-null
str must contain zero or more lat:lng pairs separated by commas; whitespace allowed

The human-readable format is not designed to preserve full precision; do not use for durable storage

functions.name: s2textformat::MakeLatLngOrDie

functions.name: s2textformat::MakeLatLng

functions.name: s2textformat::MakeLatLngRectOrDie

str must match the format "f/dd..d"
Face digit must be in [0-5]; child digits must be in [0-3]

Face digit must be in [0-5]; child digits must be in [0-3]
On invalid input the function terminates the process

functions.name: s2textformat::MakeCellUnion
functions.description: Parses a comma-separated list of S2CellIds in the debug format and writes the normalized S2CellUnion to *cell_union. Returns true on success, false on failure.
requirements: cell_union must be non-null
str must be a comma-separated list of items each matching "f/dd..d"
Face digit must be in [0-5]; child digits must be in [0-3]
Caller must check the boolean return value before using *cell_union

debug_override controls S2Debug checks; pass a valid S2Debug enum value

functions.name: s2textformat::MakePolylineOrDie

debug_override must be a valid S2Debug enum value
On invalid input the function terminates the process

functions.signature: [[nodiscard]] bool s2textformat::MakePolyline(absl::string_view str, std::unique_ptr<S2Polyline>* polyline, S2Debug debug_override = S2Debug::ALLOW)
functions.description: Parses a sequence of latitude-longitude coordinates in degrees and constructs an S2Polyline. Returns true on success and writes into *polyline; otherwise returns false.

str must be a comma-separated sequence of lat:lng coordinate pairs

debug_override must be a valid S2Debug enum value
Caller must check the boolean return value before using *polyline

functions.name: s2textformat::MakeLaxPolylineOrDie
functions.description: Parses a sequence of latitude-longitude coordinates in degrees and returns an S2LaxPolylineShape. Crashes on invalid input.
requirements: str must be a comma-separated sequence of lat:lng coordinate pairs
Coordinates must be parseable floating-point numbers
On invalid input the function terminates the process

functions.name: s2textformat::MakeLaxPolyline
functions.description: Parses a sequence of latitude-longitude coordinates in degrees and constructs an S2LaxPolylineShape. Returns true on success; otherwise returns false.
requirements: lax_polyline must be non-null
str must be a comma-separated sequence of lat:lng coordinate pairs
Coordinates must be parseable floating-point numbers
Caller must check the boolean return value before using *lax_polyline

functions.name: s2textformat::MakePolygonOrDie
functions.description: Parses one or more loops (separated by ';') of latitude-longitude coordinates in degrees and returns a newly allocated S2Polygon. Loops are automatically normalized (inverted if necessary) so they enclose at most half the sphere. Supports "", "empty" for empty polygons and "full" for the full polygon. Crashes on invalid input.

functions.name: s2textformat::MakePolygon

requirements: polygon must be non-null
str format: loops as comma-separated lat:lng coordinate lists; loops separated by ';'; may be empty string/"empty" or "full"
Coordinates must be parseable floating-point numbers
Whitespace is ignored
debug_override must be a valid S2Debug enum value
Caller must check the boolean return value before using *polygon

Coordinates must be parseable floating-point numbers
On invalid input the function terminates the process

functions.name: s2textformat::MakeVerbatimPolygon
functions.description: Parses loops like MakePolygon but does not normalize them, returning exactly what is specified in an S2Polygon. Returns true on success; otherwise false.
requirements: polygon must be non-null
str format: loops as comma-separated lat:lng coordinate lists; loops separated by ';'
Coordinates must be parseable floating-point numbers
Caller must check the boolean return value before using *polygon

functions.name: s2textformat::MakeLaxPolygonOrDie
functions.description: Parses a polygon like MakePolygon but requires each loop to be oriented so that the interior is on the left, and allows degeneracies. "full" denotes the full polygon and "" or "empty" denote the empty polygon. Crashes on invalid input.
requirements: str format: loops separated by ';' composed of comma-separated lat:lng pairs
Loops must be oriented with interior on the left
Degenerate loops/polygons are allowed
Keywords: "full" for full polygon; "" or "empty" for empty polygon
On invalid input the function terminates the process

functions.name: s2textformat::MakeLaxPolygon
functions.description: Parses a polygon into an S2LaxPolygonShape. Loops must be left-oriented; degeneracies supported. Supports "full", and "" or "empty" for empty. Returns true on success; otherwise false.
requirements: lax_polygon must be non-null
str format: loops separated by ';' composed of comma-separated lat:lng pairs
Loops must be oriented with interior on the left
Degenerate loops/polygons are allowed
Caller must check the boolean return value before using *lax_polygon

functions.name: s2textformat::MakeIndexOrDie
functions.description: Parses a composite geometry description into a MutableS2ShapeIndex using the format "point1|point2|... # line1|line2|... # polygon1|polygon2|...". Points are lat:lngs; polylines are comma-separated sequences; polygons are groups of loops with loops separated by ';'. Whitespace is ignored. Empty polygons must be specified as "empty". Loops should be oriented with interior on the left; degeneracies allowed. Crashes on invalid input.
requirements: str must use the three-section format with '#' separators: points # polylines # polygons
Within each section, geometries are separated by '|'
Polylines: vertices are comma-separated lat:lng pairs
Polygons: loops for a polygon are separated by ';'; use "empty" for empty polygons; "full" allowed
Whitespace is ignored; because of this, empty polygons cannot be encoded as empty string—use "empty"
Loops should be directed so the interior is on the left; loops can be degenerate
On invalid input the function terminates the process

functions.name: s2textformat::MakeIndex
functions.description: Parses a composite geometry description (same format as MakeIndexOrDie) and constructs a MutableS2ShapeIndex containing points, polylines, and polygons. Returns true on success; otherwise false.
requirements: index must be non-null
str must follow the points # polylines # polygons format with '|' and ';' separators
Use "empty" to denote empty polygons; "full" allowed
Whitespace is ignored
Loops should be directed so the interior is on the left; loops can be degenerate
Caller must check the boolean return value before using *index

functions.name: S2Builder::SnapFunction::kMaxSnapRadius
functions.description: Returns the maximum supported snap radius for a SnapFunction (approximately 70 degrees, ~7800km on Earth). Usage: to validate or clamp snap radii when configuring snapping.

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::snap_function
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the currently configured SnapFunction used by S2Builder for vertex snapping and separation guarantees.

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::set_snap_function
functions.description: Sets the SnapFunction used for snapping behavior. The function object is deep-copied via SnapFunction::Clone(), so temporaries are safe. Use this to configure discrete snap targets (e.g., E7 grid) and snap radius.

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::edge_snap_radius
functions.description: Returns the maximum distance from snapped edge vertices to the original edge. Normally equals snap_function().snap_radius(); if split_crossing_edges() is true, the effective edge snap radius is increased by S2::kIntersectionError.

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::max_edge_deviation
functions.description: Returns the maximum distance any point along an edge can move during snapping. It is slightly larger (≤10% more) than edge_snap_radius() because a geodesic edge’s midpoint can move more than its endpoints.

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::split_crossing_edges
functions.description: Returns whether crossing edge pairs should be detected and split by inserting intersection vertices. Enables robust elimination of crossings during snapping.

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::set_split_crossing_edges
functions.description: Enables or disables splitting of crossing edge pairs by inserting intersection vertices. When enabled, intersection_tolerance() is treated as at least S2::kIntersectionError.

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::intersection_tolerance
functions.description: Returns the maximum allowable distance between a user-added intersection vertex (via AddIntersection) and the edge(s) it is intended to snap to. When split_crossing_edges() is true, the returned value is max(user_value, S2::kIntersectionError).

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::set_intersection_tolerance
functions.description: Sets the tolerance used for user-specified intersection points (and edge tessellation points) so they are considered during snapping even with zero snap radius. Only affects edges (not vertex-vertex snapping).
requirements: intersection_tolerance must be non-negative (>= S1Angle::Zero())

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::simplify_edge_chains
functions.description: Returns whether nearly straight chains of short edges should be simplified into longer edges while preserving snapping/error guarantees.

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::set_simplify_edge_chains
functions.description: Enables or disables simplification of nearly straight edge chains. Enabling this also forces options.idempotent() to false because simplification is not idempotent across runs.
requirements: Requires a non-zero snap radius to have any effect (per class documentation)

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::idempotent
functions.description: Returns whether snapping is applied only when the input already violates the output guarantees (idempotent behavior). If false, geometry within snap_radius may be merged even if already valid.

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::set_idempotent
functions.description: Sets whether snapping should be idempotent. Typically left true unless simplifying edge chains (which forces it false).

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::memory_tracker
functions.description: Returns the S2MemoryTracker used to track S2Builder’s internal allocations, or nullptr if tracking is disabled.

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::set_memory_tracker
functions.description: Sets the S2MemoryTracker to account for S2Builder’s internal memory usage and optionally enforce a memory limit.
requirements: If a limit is set on the tracker and exceeded during Build, Build() may fail with S2Error::RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::Options
functions.description: Default-constructs an Options object with default settings (identity snap function with zero radius, no crossing split, no simplification, idempotent=true, no memory tracker).

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::Options
functions.description: Constructs Options using the provided SnapFunction (deep-copied). Convenient when choosing a particular snapping scheme and radius.

functions.name: S2Builder::Options::operator=
functions.description: Assigns from another Options instance, copying its configuration (including a deep copy of the SnapFunction).

functions.name: S2Builder::AddPoint

functions.name: S2Builder::AddPolyline

No loop may be empty; the full loop may appear only in a full polygon.

After the call, ownership transfers to the OwningShape.

functions.name: S2Polyline::OwningShape::Init
functions.description: Decodes an S2Polyline from decoder, initializes this shape to own it, and returns true on success.
requirements: decoder must not be nullptr.
On success, this object takes ownership of the newly decoded polyline.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::Options::max_cells
functions.description: Returns the configured maximum number of cells allowed in generated coverings. Used by S2RegionCoverer to bound approximation size and work.
requirements: No arguments; callable on a valid Options instance.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::Options::set_max_cells
functions.description: Sets the desired maximum number of cells in generated coverings. Higher values allow tighter coverings but increase work; up to 6 cells may still be returned if needed, and min_level takes priority over this limit.
requirements: Parameter max_cells is an integer; no explicit minimum/maximum is enforced by the interface.
Callers should be aware that values < 4 can yield very loose coverings (not a hard requirement, but important usage note).

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::Options::min_level
functions.description: Returns the minimum S2 cell level that coverings may use. Cells below this level will not be used even if it increases the number of cells required.
requirements: No arguments; callable on a valid Options instance.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::Options::set_min_level
functions.description: Sets the minimum S2 cell level for coverings. Cells below this level are never used (except interior coverings make no completeness guarantees).
requirements: min_level must be <= current max_level (REQUIRES: min_level() <= max_level()).
min_level is an integer level in the range [0, S2CellId::kMaxLevel] (implied by level definition).

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::Options::max_level
functions.description: Returns the maximum S2 cell level that coverings may use.
requirements: No arguments; callable on a valid Options instance.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::Options::set_max_level
functions.description: Sets the maximum S2 cell level for coverings.
requirements: max_level must be >= current min_level (REQUIRES: min_level() <= max_level()).
max_level is an integer level in the range [0, S2CellId::kMaxLevel] (implied by level definition).

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::Options::set_fixed_level
functions.description: Convenience setter that makes coverings use exactly the given level by setting both min_level and max_level to level.
requirements: level is an integer level in the range [0, S2CellId::kMaxLevel] (implied by level definition).

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::Options::level_mod
functions.description: Returns the level modulus constraint. Only cells where (level - min_level) is a multiple of this value are permitted in coverings.
requirements: No arguments; callable on a valid Options instance.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::Options::set_level_mod
functions.description: Sets the level modulus constraint, effectively increasing the branching factor of the S2 cell hierarchy used for coverings.
requirements: level_mod must be one of {1, 2, 3}.
Only cells where (level - min_level) % level_mod == 0 will be used.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::Options::true_max_level
functions.description: Returns the maximum level that will actually be used in coverings, i.e., the largest level L such that L <= max_level and (L - min_level) % level_mod == 0.
requirements: No arguments; callable on a valid Options instance.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::S2RegionCoverer
functions.description: Constructs a region coverer with the given options. Use to configure covering behavior (max_cells, min/max levels, level_mod).
requirements: options must refer to a valid Options object; it is copied into the coverer.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::S2RegionCoverer
functions.description: Default-constructs a region coverer with default options (e.g., max_cells = Options::kDefaultMaxCells, min_level = 0, max_level = S2CellId::kMaxLevel, level_mod = 1). Options can be adjusted via mutable_options().
requirements: No arguments.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator. Replaces this object's state by moving from another S2RegionCoverer.
requirements: Source object must be an rvalue (movable).
Noexcept: move assignment will not throw.
The target object must be a valid S2RegionCoverer instance.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::~S2RegionCoverer
functions.description: Destructor for S2RegionCoverer. Releases any internal resources; typical use is automatic via RAII.
requirements: Object must have been constructed; no special teardown required by callers.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::options
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the current Options. Modify options between coverings using mutable_options().
requirements: Callable on a valid S2RegionCoverer instance; returned reference remains valid as long as the coverer exists and options are not replaced.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::mutable_options
functions.description: Returns a mutable pointer to the current Options, allowing in-place configuration changes that affect subsequent coverings.
requirements: Do not keep the returned pointer beyond the lifetime of the coverer.
Callers must honor Options invariants (e.g., min_level <= max_level, level_mod in {1,2,3}).

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::GetCovering
functions.description: Generates a covering S2CellUnion that covers the given region while respecting the current options (max_cells, min_level, max_level, level_mod). The result may not be normalized if min_level > 0 or level_mod > 1.
requirements: region must be a valid S2Region object and remain alive for the duration of the call.
Resulting S2CellUnion size will be bounded by options except in documented edge cases (e.g., up to 6 cells may be necessary).

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::GetCovering
functions.signature: void S2RegionCoverer::GetCovering(const S2Region& region, std::vector<S2CellId>* covering)
functions.description: Fills 'covering' with a set of S2CellIds that cover the region. Equivalent to the S2CellUnion overload but reuses the provided vector to avoid allocations.
requirements: covering must be non-null.
region must be a valid S2Region object and remain alive for the duration of the call.
Output may not be normalized if min_level > 0 or level_mod > 1.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::GetInteriorCovering
functions.description: Generates an interior covering S2CellUnion whose cells are entirely contained within the region while satisfying current options. Interior coverings may be empty and make no completeness guarantees.
requirements: region must be a valid S2Region object and remain alive for the duration of the call.
For performance, callers are advised to set a max_level for small-area regions (usage note).

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::GetInteriorCovering
functions.description: Fills 'interior' with S2CellIds whose cells are entirely contained within the region, subject to options. May produce an empty result.
requirements: interior must be non-null.
region must be a valid S2Region object and remain alive for the duration of the call.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::GetFastCovering
functions.signature: void S2RegionCoverer::GetFastCovering(const S2Region& region, std::vector<S2CellId>* covering)
functions.description: Computes a faster but looser covering. Respects max_cells, min_level, max_level, and level_mod, but does not exploit large max_cells values (always returns a small number of cells). Useful as a seed for recursive subdivision.
requirements: covering must be non-null.
region must be valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::GetSimpleCovering
functions.signature: static void S2RegionCoverer::GetSimpleCovering(const S2Region& region, const S2Point& start, int level, std::vector<S2CellId>* output)
functions.description: Given a connected region and a starting point on its boundary or interior, returns (in arbitrary order) the set of cells at the specified level that cover the region. Intended for certain shapes (e.g., long narrow regions). May be slower than GetCovering for many region types.
requirements: region should be connected (as assumed by the algorithm).
start must lie on the region boundary or inside the region.
level must be a valid S2 cell level (integer in [0, S2CellId::kMaxLevel]).
output must be non-null.
Output cells are all at 'level' and unordered.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::FloodFill
functions.signature: static void S2RegionCoverer::FloodFill(const S2Region& region, S2CellId start, std::vector<S2CellId>* output)
functions.description: Returns all edge-connected cells, at the same level as 'start', that intersect 'region', in arbitrary order. Starting from 'start', it performs a flood fill over neighboring cells.
requirements: start must be a valid S2CellId; the level of all output cells equals start.level().
region must be valid for the duration of the call.
output must be non-null.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::IsCanonical
functions.description: Checks whether the given covering conforms to the current options. Validates IDs, ordering, non-overlap, level constraints (min_level, max_level, level_mod), max_cells constraint via ancestors, and ensures no group of children could be replaced by their ancestor.
requirements: covering must contain valid S2CellIds.
S2CellIds must be sorted and non-overlapping.
Cell levels must satisfy min_level(), max_level(), and level_mod().
If covering.size() > max_cells(), there must be no two cells with a common ancestor at min_level() or higher.
There must be no sequence of cells that could be replaced by an ancestor (e.g., all 4 children with level_mod==1).

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::IsCanonical
functions.description: Same as the S2CellUnion overload, but operates directly on a vector of S2CellIds.
requirements: Vector entries must be valid S2CellIds.
S2CellIds must be sorted and non-overlapping.
Cell levels must satisfy min_level(), max_level(), and level_mod().
If covering.size() > max_cells(), there must be no two cells with a common ancestor at min_level() or higher.
There must be no sequence of cells that could be replaced by an ancestor (e.g., all 4 children with level_mod==1).

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::CanonicalizeCovering
functions.description: Returns a version of 'covering' that conforms to current options (max_cells, min_level, max_level, level_mod). Input may be unsorted, overlapping, etc.; the result is adjusted and normalized.
requirements: Input S2CellUnion may contain arbitrary S2CellIds; no preconditions.
Callers should expect that cells may be replaced by ancestors or filtered to meet options.

functions.name: S2RegionCoverer::CanonicalizeCovering
functions.description: In-place canonicalization of a vector of S2CellIds to conform to current options. Adjusts cell levels, removes overlaps, and normalizes as needed.
requirements: covering must be non-null; may contain arbitrary S2CellIds before the call.

functions.name: S2Loop::S2Loop
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates an uninitialized loop; you must call Init() or Decode() before use.
requirements: Must call Init(absl::Span<const S2Point>) or Decode(Decoder*) before using other functionality.

functions.name: S2Loop::S2Loop
functions.description: Move constructor. Transfers the internal state of another S2Loop into this one.

functions.name: S2Loop::S2Loop
functions.description: Convenience constructor that initializes the loop from a vertex span by calling Init(vertices).

functions.name: S2Loop::S2Loop
functions.description: Constructor that sets a debug override level and initializes the loop from vertices. Use to disable automatic validity checking controlled by --s2debug.
requirements: Same vertex requirements as Init(vertices).
Use set_s2debug_override(S2Debug) equivalent semantics: automatic validity checks may be disabled if override is S2Debug::DISABLE.

functions.name: S2Loop::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator. Replaces this loop’s contents by moving from another S2Loop.
requirements: After move, the source S2Loop is left in a valid but unspecified state (standard C++ move semantics).

functions.name: S2Loop::Init
functions.description: Initializes or reinitializes the loop with the given vertices; the last vertex is implicitly connected to the first.
requirements: All points should be unit length.
Loops must have at least 3 vertices (except for kEmpty() and kFull()).
Adjacent vertices must not be antipodal; non-adjacent edges must not intersect; no duplicate vertices (not enforced in optimized code).
May be called multiple times on the same object.

functions.name: S2Loop::kEmpty
functions.description: Returns a special 1-vertex span that, when used to construct or initialize a loop, represents the empty loop (contains no points, has no boundary).
requirements: If serialized lossily, its position must not move by 90 degrees or more to preserve identity as empty (as documented).

functions.name: S2Loop::kFull
functions.description: Returns a special 1-vertex span that, when used to construct or initialize a loop, represents the full loop (contains all points, has no boundary).
requirements: If serialized lossily, its position must not move by 90 degrees or more to preserve identity as full (as documented).

functions.name: S2Loop::~S2Loop
functions.description: Destructor for S2Loop. Releases resources associated with the loop.

functions.name: S2Loop::set_s2debug_override
functions.description: Overrides the automatic validity checks controlled by the --s2debug flag for subsequent Init() or Decode() calls.
requirements: Setting persists across Init() and Decode().

functions.name: S2Loop::s2debug_override
functions.description: Returns the current S2Debug override setting controlling automatic validity checks.

functions.name: S2Loop::IsValid
functions.description: Returns true if the loop is valid (no duplicate vertices, no self-intersections, no 180° edges, etc.). When --s2debug is enabled, Init() checks validity automatically.

functions.name: S2Loop::FindValidationError
functions.description: If the loop is invalid, sets 'error' with details and returns true; otherwise returns false and leaves 'error' unchanged.
requirements: error must not be nullptr.

functions.name: S2Loop::num_vertices
functions.description: Returns the number of vertices in the loop. For empty/full loops this is 1 by definition.

functions.name: S2Loop::vertex
functions.description: Returns vertex i with support for indexing into a duplicated range [0, 2*num_vertices()) that maps into [0, num_vertices()). Useful for seamless edge iteration.
requirements: 0 <= i < 2 * num_vertices() (REQUIRES).

functions.name: S2Loop::oriented_vertex
functions.description: Returns vertex i in forward order for shells and reverse order for holes, over the range [0, 2*num_vertices()). Ensures interior is to the left of the vertex chain.
requirements: 0 <= i < 2 * num_vertices() (REQUIRES).

functions.name: S2Loop::vertices_span
functions.description: Returns an S2PointLoopSpan view over the loop vertices for use with s2loop_measures.h helper functions.

functions.name: S2Loop::is_empty
functions.description: Returns true if this is the special empty loop (1-vertex loop not containing S2::Origin).

functions.name: S2Loop::is_full
functions.description: Returns true if this is the special full loop (1-vertex loop containing S2::Origin).

functions.name: S2Loop::is_empty_or_full
functions.description: Returns true if this loop is either the special empty or full loop (i.e., has exactly one vertex).

functions.name: S2Loop::depth
functions.description: Returns the nesting depth of the loop within a polygon (0 for outer shells, 1 for holes, etc.). Used by S2Polygon.

functions.name: S2Loop::set_depth
functions.description: Sets the loop's nesting depth within its containing polygon. Used by S2Polygon.

functions.name: S2Loop::is_hole
functions.description: Returns true if the loop represents a hole in its containing polygon (depth is odd).

functions.name: S2Loop::sign
functions.description: Returns -1 if the loop represents a hole, +1 otherwise.

functions.name: S2Loop::IsNormalized
functions.description: Returns true if the loop area is at most 2π. Degenerate loops are handled consistently with s2pred::Sign().

functions.name: S2Loop::Normalize
functions.description: Inverts the loop if necessary so that its enclosed area is at most 2π.

functions.name: S2Loop::Invert
functions.description: Reverses the vertex order, complementing the region represented by the loop.

functions.name: S2Loop::GetArea
functions.description: Returns the area of the loop interior in steradians, in [0, 4π].

functions.name: S2Loop::GetCentroid
functions.description: Returns the true centroid of the loop multiplied by its area (not normalized). May lie outside the loop.

functions.name: S2Loop::GetCurvature
functions.description: Returns the geodesic curvature (sum of turn angles) of the loop. Positive for CCW, negative for CW, zero for great circles. Equals 2π minus area.

functions.name: S2Loop::GetCurvatureMaxError
functions.description: Returns the maximum error bound associated with GetCurvature() for this loop.

functions.name: S2Loop::GetDistance
functions.description: Returns the distance from point x to the loop interior. Returns S1Angle::Infinity() for an empty loop.
requirements: x should be unit length.

functions.name: S2Loop::GetDistanceToBoundary
functions.description: Returns the distance from point x to the loop boundary. Returns Infinity for empty or full loops (no boundary).
requirements: x should be unit length.

functions.name: S2Loop::Project
functions.description: If x is inside the loop, returns x; otherwise returns the closest point to x on the loop boundary. For empty loops, returns x.
requirements: x should be unit length.

functions.name: S2Loop::ProjectToBoundary
functions.description: Returns the closest point on the loop boundary to x. For empty or full loops (no boundary), returns x.
requirements: x should be unit length.

functions.name: S2Loop::Contains
functions.description: Returns true if the region contained by this loop is a superset of the region contained by loop b. Tests for containment including boundary cases and crossings.

functions.name: S2Loop::Contains
functions.description: Returns true if this loop contains the given S2Cell (S2Region interface).

functions.name: S2Loop::Contains
functions.description: Returns true if the given point is contained by the loop. This method uses a simple brute force approach initially; point need not be normalized.
requirements: The point p does not need to be normalized (as documented).

functions.name: S2Loop::Intersects
functions.description: Returns true if the regions contained by this loop and loop b intersect.

functions.name: S2Loop::Equals
functions.description: Returns true if two loops have the same vertices in the same linear order (no cyclic rotation allowed).

functions.name: S2Loop::BoundaryEquals
functions.description: Returns true if two loops have the same boundary (same vertices in the same cyclic order). Empty and full loops are considered to have different boundaries.

functions.name: S2Loop::BoundaryApproxEquals
functions.signature: bool S2Loop::BoundaryApproxEquals(const S2Loop& b, S1Angle max_error) const
functions.description: Returns true if two loops have the same boundary up to vertex perturbations no more than max_error and in the same cyclic order.

functions.name: S2Loop::BoundaryNear
functions.signature: bool S2Loop::BoundaryNear(const S2Loop& b, S1Angle max_error) const
functions.description: Returns true if the two loop boundaries stay within max_error of each other along their entire lengths (parameterized without backtracking). Loop sizes may differ.

functions.name: S2Loop::GetSurfaceIntegral
functions.signature: template <class T> T S2Loop::GetSurfaceIntegral(T f_tri(const S2Point&, const S2Point&, const S2Point&)) const
functions.description: Computes the oriented surface integral of a quantity f over the loop interior, given a triangle integral callback f_tri(A,B,C) that returns the oriented integral over spherical triangle ABC.

The default constructor for T must initialize to zero.

functions.name: S2Loop::MakeRegularLoop
functions.signature: static std::unique_ptr<S2Loop> S2Loop::MakeRegularLoop(const Matrix3x3_d& frame, S1Angle radius, int num_vertices)
functions.description: Builds a regular polygon loop centered on the z-axis of 'frame', with the first vertex in the +x direction of 'frame', radius from the center, and num_vertices vertices (useful for tests/rotation).

functions.name: S2Loop::SpaceUsed

functions.name: S2Loop::GetCapBound
functions.description: Returns a conservative spherical cap bound that contains the loop. May include extra padding compared to the true bound.

functions.name: S2Loop::GetRectBound
functions.description: Returns a conservative latitude-longitude rectangle bound that tightly contains the loop.

functions.name: S2Loop::GetCellUnionBound

functions.name: S2Loop::MayIntersect

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid S2 cell token strings (and some edge/near-edge cases)
# suitable for S2CellId::FromToken and AbslParseFlag fuzzers that consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
#
# S2 tokens are typically hexadecimal-like strings (case-insensitive) that encode the
# 64-bit cell id compactly without leading zeros. The empty string represents None().
# Lower/upper case variants are accepted. Short tokens correspond to coarse levels; longer
# ones to deeper levels. We generate a variety of lengths and special cases.

_HEX = '0123456789abcdef'
_HEX_UP = '0123456789ABCDEF'

# Precompute some interesting, valid tokens observed/used by S2:
# - Empty: None()
# - Single face ids: 0..5
# - Max-length like strings (simulate deep levels) using repeating face digits
# - Mixed-case variants
_INTERESTING_VALID = [
    '',              # None()
    '0','1','2','3','4','5',  # Faces
    'X',             # Often used as a sentinel token by S2 for Sentinel()
]

# Generate a plausible valid token of a given length using hex digits.
# While exact S2 ToToken format is internal, it is hexadecimal-like and case-insensitive.
# We ensure no leading zeros for non-empty tokens to mimic typical ToToken behavior.

def _rand_valid_token(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    if length <= 0:
        return ''
    # First char avoid '0' sometimes to mimic trimming, but allow occasionally.
    first_pool = _HEX[1:] if rng.random() < 0.8 else _HEX
    s = rng.choice(first_pool)
    if length > 1:
        for _ in range(length-1):
            s += rng.choice(_HEX)
    # Randomly apply uppercase/lowercase/mixed
    style = rng.randint(0,2)
    if style == 0:
        return s
    elif style == 1:
        return s.upper()
    else:
        # mixed
        return ''.join(c.upper() if rng.random() < 0.5 else c for c in s)

# Generate tokens that are still likely valid but exercise boundaries:
# - Very short/very long
# - With minimal/maximum nibble usage
# - Alternating patterns

def _pattern_token(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    patterns = []
    # Alternating 0 and f
    n = rng.randint(1, 16)
    patterns.append(('0f'*n)[:n])
    patterns.append(('f0'*n)[:n])
    # Repeating a face digit
    face = rng.choice('012345')
    patterns.append(face * rng.randint(1, 16))
    # Ramp pattern
    base = ''.join(_HEX[i%16] for i in range(rng.randint(1,16)))
    patterns.append(base)
    tok = rng.choice(patterns)
    # Random case
    if rng.random() < 0.33:
        tok = tok.upper()
    elif rng.random() < 0.66:
        tok = ''.join(c.upper() if rng.random()<0.5 else c for c in tok)
    return tok

# Include a few intentionally unusual-but-accepted forms to exercise parsers:
# - Strings with surrounding whitespace trimmed by Abseil flag parser
# - Plus/minus with hex (some parsers reject; keeps diversity). We keep primarily valid.

def _decorate_token(rng: random.Random, tok: str) -> str:
    # Mostly return plain tokens; sometimes add harmless whitespace
    p = rng.random()
    if p < 0.15:
        ws_left = ' ' * rng.randint(0, 2) + ('\t' if rng.random()<0.5 else '')
        ws_right = ('\n' if rng.random()<0.5 else '') + ' ' * rng.randint(0, 2)
        return ws_left + tok + ws_right
    return tok

# Build a corpus of candidate tokens and pick one based on seed

def _choose_token(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choices: List[str] = []
    # Seed with interesting constants
    choices.extend(_INTERESTING_VALID)
    # Some realistic valid lengths: 1..16
    for _ in range(10):
        choices.append(_rand_valid_token(rng, rng.randint(1, 16)))
    # Include a couple of longer tokens up to 24 nibbles to mimic deep levels
    for _ in range(3):
        choices.append(_rand_valid_token(rng, rng.randint(17, 24)))
    # Pattern-based
    for _ in range(5):
        choices.append(_pattern_token(rng))
    tok = rng.choice(choices)
    tok = _decorate_token(rng, tok)
    return tok

# The fuzzer expects bytes; we return UTF-8 encoding of the chosen token string.

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    token = _choose_token(rng)
    # Ensure size cap
    if len(token) > 4096:
        token = token[:4096]
    return token.encode('utf-8')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for S2CellId debug strings. S2CellId::FromDebugString typically accepts
# formats like:
#  - "f" (face 0..5)
#  - "f/" (face only)
#  - "f/dd..d" where d are digits 0..3 representing child positions along the
#    Hilbert curve (level up to S2::kMaxCellLevel, commonly 30), but the parser
#    is generally tolerant. It may also accept tokens like "face:ij.." variants
#    in some builds, but we stick to the documented debug form to maximize valid parses.
#
# The fuzzer stub sometimes prepends a valid face and slash; our payload should
# therefore focus on providing interesting suffixes after "f/", but we also
# generate complete self-contained strings to succeed when the stub uses our
# buffer directly.

MAX_LEVEL = 30  # typical S2 max cell level

def _rand_face(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return str(rng.randrange(0, 6))

def _hilbert_digits(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randrange(min_len, max_len + 1)
    return ''.join(rng.choice('0123') for _ in range(n))

def _cases(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []

    # 1) Minimal valid: face only
    out.append(_rand_face(rng))

    # 2) Face with slash only (root of a face)
    out.append(_rand_face(rng) + "/")

    # 3) Face with a small number of digits (levels 1..5)
    out.append(_rand_face(rng) + "/" + _hilbert_digits(rng, 1, 5))

    # 4) Medium depth
    out.append(_rand_face(rng) + "/" + _hilbert_digits(rng, 6, 12))

    # 5) Deep cell close to max level
    out.append(_rand_face(rng) + "/" + _hilbert_digits(rng, 20, MAX_LEVEL))

    # 6) Edge cases: all same digit
    for d in '0123':
        out.append(_rand_face(rng) + "/" + d * rng.randrange(1, 16))

    # 7) Empty string (exercise failure path)
    out.append("")

    # 8) Whitespace padded valid strings
    s = _rand_face(rng) + "/" + _hilbert_digits(rng, 1, 8)
    out.append("  " + s)
    out.append(s + "  ")

    # 9) Multiple segments separated by spaces (parser may stop at first token)
    out.append(_rand_face(rng) + "/" + _hilbert_digits(rng, 1, 6) + " " + _rand_face(rng))

    # 10) Just digits after slash of maximum reasonable length
    out.append(_rand_face(rng) + "/" + _hilbert_digits(rng, MAX_LEVEL, MAX_LEVEL))

    return out

def _choose_payload(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choices = _cases(rng)

    # Also include a few randomly mixed but still valid patterns
    for _ in range(5):
        face = _rand_face(rng)
        # 50% chance to include slash
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            s = face + "/" + _hilbert_digits(rng, 0, MAX_LEVEL)  # allow empty after slash
        else:
            s = face
        choices.append(s)

    return rng.choice(choices)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # The fuzz harness uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR once. We provide one debug string.
    # Keep it under the 4096-byte limit; our strings are tiny.
    payload = _choose_payload(rng)

    # Return as UTF-8 bytes. No trailing NUL to keep it as pure string content.
    return payload.encode('utf-8')

# Target data type: arbitrary string

    return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))

def _repeat_pattern(pattern: bytes, total: int) -> bytes:
    if not pattern:
        return b""
    reps = (total + len(pattern) - 1) // len(pattern)
    return (pattern * reps)[:total]

def _utf8_message(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a UTF-8 string by joining random fragments with separators
    parts = []
    target = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    while len("".join(parts).encode('utf-8')) < target:
        frag = rng.choice(_UTF8_FRAGMENTS)
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            frag += rng.choice([" ", " - ", " | ", " :: "])

    s = "".join(parts)
    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    return b[:max_len]

def _json_like(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:

    code = rng.randint(-10**6, 10**6)
    msg = rng.choice(_UTF8_FRAGMENTS) + rng.choice(["", " details", " cause"])  # utf8
    status = rng.choice(["OK", "ERROR", "UNKNOWN", "CANCELLED", "DATA_LOSS"])  # ascii

        s = tmpl % (code, msg)
    elif tmpl.count("%s") == 2:
        s = tmpl % (status, msg, code)

def _xml_like(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    tmpl = rng.choice(_XML_TEMPLATES)
    code = rng.randint(0, 9999)
    typ = rng.choice(["info", "warning", "error", "fatal"])
    msg = rng.choice(_UTF8_FRAGMENTS)

    while sum(len(c) for c in chunks) < length:
        choice = rng.random()
        remain = length - sum(len(c) for c in chunks)
        take = rng.randint(1, max(1, min(64, remain)))
        if choice < 0.2:
            chunks.append(b"\x00" * take)
        elif choice < 0.4:
            chunks.append(bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(take)))
        elif choice < 0.7:
            chunks.append(_repeat_pattern(rng.choice(_ASCII_WORDS), take))
        else:
            # sample from control set
            chunks.append(bytes(rng.choice(_CONTROL_BYTES) for _ in range(take)))
    return b"".join(chunks)[:length]

def _compressed_like(rng: random.Random, base: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Create data that either is compressed or looks compressed
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        comp = zlib.compress(base, level=rng.choice([1, 6, 9]))
        return comp[:_MAX]
    # Otherwise, craft a zlib-like header then noise
    hdr = b"\x78" + bytes([rng.choice([0x01, 0x5E, 0x9C, 0xDA])])
    body = _binary_like(rng, min(512, max(32, len(base))))
    return (hdr + body)[:_MAX]

def _pathy(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 8)):
        frag = rng.choice(_ASCII_WORDS).decode('ascii')
        parts.append(frag)
    sep = rng.choice(["/", "\\\\"])
    pref = rng.choice(["", "/", "./", "../", "C:\\", "~/"])
    s = pref + sep.join(parts)
    return s.encode('utf-8')

def _with_prefix_suffix(rng: random.Random, core: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Add common prefixes/suffixes
    prefixes = [b"", b"ERROR:", b"WARN:", b"[S2] ", b"(code=", b"<tag>"]
    suffixes = [b"", b"\n", b"\r\n", b"\x00", b")", b"</tag>"]
    pre = rng.choice(prefixes)
    suf = rng.choice(suffixes)
    out = pre + core + suf
    return out[:_MAX]

_generators = []

def _init_generators():
    global _generators
    if _generators:
        return
    _generators = [
        lambda rng: b"",  # empty
        lambda rng: b"\n",  # newline only
        lambda rng: b"\x00",  # single NUL
        lambda rng: rng.choice(_ASCII_WORDS),
        lambda rng: _with_prefix_suffix(rng, rng.choice(_ASCII_WORDS)),
        lambda rng: _utf8_message(rng, 8, 128),
        lambda rng: _utf8_message(rng, 256, 1024),
        lambda rng: _json_like(rng),
        lambda rng: _xml_like(rng),
        lambda rng: _sql_like(rng),
        lambda rng: _pathy(rng),
        lambda rng: _with_prefix_suffix(rng, _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 64))),
        lambda rng: _repeat_pattern(b"A" * rng.randint(1, 8), rng.randint(16, 1024)),
        lambda rng: _repeat_pattern(b"\x00\xff", rng.randint(16, 1024)),
        lambda rng: _binary_like(rng, rng.randint(1, 2048)),
        lambda rng: _compressed_like(rng, _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(64, 512))),
        lambda rng: _compressed_like(rng, _binary_like(rng, rng.randint(64, 512))),
        lambda rng: (b";".join(rng.choice(_ASCII_WORDS) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 40))))[:_MAX],
        lambda rng: (b"\n".join(rng.choice(_PATHS) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 40))))[:_MAX],
        lambda rng: _with_prefix_suffix(rng, _CONTROL_BYTES[:rng.randint(1, len(_CONTROL_BYTES))]),
    ]

_init_generators()

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = _rand_rng(seed)
    choice_idx = rng.randrange(len(_generators))
    data = _generators[choice_idx](rng)
    # Occasionally mix in additional context lines to increase variety
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and len(data) < _MAX:
        extras = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            g = rng.choice(_generators)
            extras.append(g(rng))
        sep = rng.choice([b"\n", b"\x00", b" ", b"\n---\n"]) if rng.random() < 0.8 else b""
        data = sep.join([data] + extras)
    return data[:_MAX]
